newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French, German shares at record despite Dow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French, German shares at record despite Dow.

text.p: European stock markets rose on Thursday despite a roller-coaster ride on Wall Street overnight, with French and German stocks marching on to record highs.

The dollar steadied after German central bank council member Reimut Jochimsen said at a dinner late on Wednesday he would not rule out a German rate cut but did not expect one. The dollar initially rose but came back and steadied on the realisation that Jochimsen did not expect a rate cut soon.

His comments came on the eve of the German Bundesbank's council meeting during the morning, but most analysts expected the central bank to keep its rates steady. The Bundesbank said it would not hold a news conference after its meeting.
Regarding European economic and monetary union (EMU), Jochimsen also warned that a lack of political integration and a fundamental difference between France and Germany were threatening the project.

France has called for a political counterweight to the future European Central Bank and for European Union-wide policies to create jobs. But Germany says job creation measures are up to national governments and argues that there can be no "European solution to unemployment."

Jochimsen's comments had little impact on European cross currency rates. Traders said the market was more focused on the Italian lira's rise to a five-month high against the mark amid speculation that Italy might lower rates.
In stocks, Paris remained in the spotlight as the CAC-40 raced to 2,888.97 points, its second consecutive record high.
